preamble: Deaffrication of the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] to the voiceless palatal stop [c] is a regional realization rather than a widespread change. It is documented in Canary Islands and Cuban Spanish, where the traditional 'ch adherente' is articulated as a fully palatal stop, and may voice to [ɟ] between vowels. In the Canaries the plosive variant is still widespread, though it alternates with the standard affricate and with a hybrid [cʃ].

examples.note: 'Boy'. The traditional Canarian 'ch adherente' is a palatal stop; intervocalic voicing gives [ɟ].
